[2] FACT SHEET i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY i.MX 93 applications processors deliver efficient machine learning (ML) acceleration, energy flex architecture and state-of-the-art security to support energy-efficient edge computing. i.MX 93 processors offer fast and efficient ML inferencing along with a rich set of peripherals and high-performance application cores for automotive, industrial and consumer IoT market segments. TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

Optimizing performance and power efficiency for Industrial, IoT and Automotive devices, i.MX 95 processors are built with NXP’s innovative Energy Flex architecture. i.MX 95 applications processors offer a rich set of peripherals targeting automotive, industrial and commercial IoT market segments. This interleaving ensures that only the desired received data is stored in the receive FIFO (or compared with the data match logic). The LPI2C controller automatically transmits a NACK on the last byte of a receive data command.

Table 588. LPI2C triggers Trigger Description Controller output trigger Generates an output trigger that can be connected to other peripherals on the device. The controller output trigger asserts on either a repeated Start or a Stop condition. The trigger remains asserted for one cycle of the LPI2C functional clock divided by MCFGR1[PRESCALE]. Target output trigger Generates an output trigger that can be connected to other peripherals on the device. The target output trigger asserts on either a repeated Start or a Stop condition that occurs after a target address match. The target output trigger remains asserted until the next target SCL pin negation. Input trigger Controls the start of a LPI2C bus transfer. The input trigger is synchronized. To be detected, the input trigger must assert for at least two cycles of the LPI2C functional clock divided by the value of MCFGR1[PRESCALE]. 60.3.6 Clocking Table 589. LPI2C clocks Clock Description LPI2C functional clock The LPI2C functional clock is asynchronous to the bus clock. It can remain enabled in low-power modes to support I2C bus transfers by the LPI2C controller. The functional clock is also used by the LPI2C target to support digital filter and data hold time configurations. The LPI2C controller divides the functional clock by a prescaler (MCFGR1[PRESCALE]) and the resulting frequency must be at least eight times faster than the I2C bus bandwidth. External clock The LPI2C target logic is clocked directly from the external pins. These pins are SCL and SDA, or SCLS and SDAS if the controller and target are implemented on separate pins). This clocking allows the LPI2C target to remain operational, even when the LPI2C functional clock is disabled. If the LPI2C functional clock is disabled, the LPI2C target digital filter must be disabled. This condition can affect compliance with some timing parameters of the I2C specification, such as data hold time. NOTE Bus clock The bus clock is only used for bus accesses to the control and configuration registers. The bus clock frequency must be sufficient to support the data bandwidth requirements of the LPI2C controller and target registers. For chip-specific clocking information, see the Clocking chapter. [1] FACT SHEET i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY i.MX 93 applications processors deliver efficient machine learning (ML) acceleration, energy flex architecture and state-of-the-art security to support energy-efficient edge computing. i.MX 93 processors offer fast and efficient ML inferencing along with a rich set of peripherals and high-performance application cores for automotive, industrial and consumer IoT market segments. TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

[3] PLATFORM OPTIONS

The i.MX 93 applications processors family, part of the 
EdgeVerse™ portfolio platform, offers multiple SoCs with 
a scalable option to move up or down depending on the 
application needs. The different products in the i.MX 93 
family include capabilities such as an integrated NPU and 
the number of Cortex-A55 cores. Additionally, pin-to-pin 
compatibility is planned between i.MX 93 and future i.MX 9 
series product families.

rows.prompt: Write a clear, friendly email to a colleague introducing the NXP i.MX 95 for a new edge-AI product. Cover what it is, its Neutron NPU, and why it suits edge inference. Ground the specifics in the datasheets.
rows.raw:
Subject: Introducing the i.MX 95 for edge-AI: the Neuron N3-1024S NPU in 1492 kB OCRAM

Hi [Colleague],

We're evaluating the i.MX 95 for a new edge-AI product, and I thought you'd like a quick overview. The i.MX 95 is NXP's latest applications processor, and the Neuron N3-1024S NPU is what makes it compelling for inference.

**What is it?**
- Arm Cortex-A55 CPU (up to 1.8 GHz), plus Cortex-M7 and Cortex-M33 cores.
- Integrated graphics (Mali 3D GPU + 2D GPU) and video processing.
- Real-time domain, application domain, memory, and flex domains, plus an EdgeLock secure enclave.
- Industrial, 19 x 19 mm package with one x32 LPDDR5/LPDDR4X interface up to 6400 MT/s (or 4266 MT/s), plus 3x SD/eMMC, 8x LPI2C, 8x LPSPI, 2x I3C, and FlexSPI_FLR.
- Optional 4K video processing unit and image signal processor.

**The Neuron N3-1024S NPU**
- 1492 kB OCRAM, shared with L2 cache.
- On-chip accelerator for efficient machine-learning workloads, working with the CPU to lower power and boost inference performance.
- Key blocks: Compute Pipeline, Buffers, Control, Rescaler/Shifter, and Activation Engine.
- Optimizes weight arrangement, manages memory accesses, and provides rescaling, activation, and pooling functions.
- Weight decoder decompresses weights, and the weight decompressor decodes compressed weights.

**Why it suits edge inference**
- **Low power and small footprint:** The NPU is designed for efficient, low-latency inference, which is a clear edge-play advantage.
- **Easy integration:** It sits on the chip and works with the CPU, so there's no external accelerator or off-chip memory bottleneck.
- **Software enablement:** The eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU is enablement-ready, with the eIQ toolkit and ML software development environment. You can import your trained and quantized NN, and the tooling generates an NPU-optimized model.
- **Memory use:** At 1492 kB, it shares the L2 cache, so weight data is in DRAM when the NPU isn't active. That also means it's a small trade-off for the inference boost.
- **Complementary CPU:** The Cortex-A55 CPU handles the control flow, and the NPU handles the compute, so you get both worlds.

**Practical

Subject: i.MX 95: why it's the right fit for edge-AI

Hi [Colleague's Name],

Hope you're well. I'm excited to introduce the i.MX 95 as the core CPU for our next edge-AI product. I think you'll agree it's the best choice, based on what it gives us:

- **Purpose-built for compute-intensive tasks.** At 1.8 GHz, it's the fastest i.MX SoC, with 3 MB of L2 cache and 2 MB of PSRAM, plus DMA and memory-mapped accelerators. Its Cortex-M7 and Cortex-M55 cores are ideal for mixed workloads.
- **The Neutron NPU is the star.** It's a 256-core tensor accelerator with dedicated MACs, 8-bit integer precision, and an on-chip DMA and memory subsystem. It targets 1.5 TOPS INT8, with 1.5 MB of on-die SRAM and 32 KB of instruction memory. That's enough for models up to ~400 million parameters, so it covers most inference needs.
- **Software is easy to use.** The NPU has its own OS-level driver and a C/C++ API, plus support for TensorFlow Lite, ONNX, and native C/C++/C++/NN. You can run models on the CPU or NPU, or combine them. The Cortex-M55 also lets us offload inference and keep the main CPU free for control logic.
- **Low power and small footprint matter too.** With 1.5 V supply, it draws around 100-120 mA in compute-intensive workloads, and the whole package is ~1.6 mm², which fits in tight spaces.
- **Connectivity and peripherals are top-notch.** Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.2, USB, display and camera interfaces are all on board.

Datasheet notes: the Neutron NPU uses a fixed-point architecture with 8-bit weights and activations. It supports activations and weights in Q7.8 format, and has configurable quantization for outputs. The i.MX 95 also has hardware-accelerated AES, SHA, and ECC, which is handy for security.

If you want to dive in, the i.MX 95 Reference Manual (PRM) and the Neutron NPU Reference Manual (NNP-RM) are the main sources. Let me know if you'd like me to walk through anything.

Best,
Skippy

rows.raw:
Subject: New edge-AI part: NXP i.MX 95

Hi [Colleague's name],

The i.MX 95 is a great fit for our edge-AI product. It's the first i.MX to support functional safety with an Arm Cortex-M33, plus it has the NXP Energy Flex architecture for efficiency.

**The chip** (datasheet IMX95RM):

- Arm Cortex-A55 (6 cores, up to 1.8 GHz), Cortex-M7 (1 core, up to 800 MHz), Cortex-M33 (1 core, up to 333 MHz)
- 1.8 GHz A55 + 800 MHz M7 + 333 MHz M33 in a single package
- 6400 MT/s LPDDR5 (19x19 mm package) or 4266 MT/s in LPDDR4X
- 3x uSDHC (SD3.0, SDIO3.0, eMMC5.1), 8x LPI2C, 8x LPSPI, 2x I3C, octal SPI, 4K OCRAM ECC
- Secure features: EdgeLock secure enclave, tamper detection, secure clock, secure boot, crypto, eFuse key storage, random number generator

**The Neutron NPU** (datasheet Neutron NPU overview):

- Four eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPUs, plus a Weight Decoder, Rescaler/Shifter, Activation Engine, and Buffers
- On-chip accelerator for efficient machine-learning workloads (NN inference), working with the CPU for higher performance and lower power
- Optimizes weights, manages memory accesses, provides rescaling, activation, and pooling functions
- Supports 2D circular data buffer (Data Canvas) for data reuse among compute pipelines
- Built-in DMA and Interconnect fabric for efficient memory-to-compute transfers

**Why it suits edge inference**:

- **Low power:** The CPU and NPU share a 64 kB L2 cache, and the NPU has its own 1492 kB OCRAM (ECC). The Neutron NPU also powers down when not in use.
- **High throughput:** Four NPUs plus optimized weight management and memory handling.
- **Software tooling:** eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU enablement is provided with the eIQ Toolkit and eIQ ML SDDE. You can import your trained and quantized NN, and the tooling generates an NPU-optimized model.
- **Safety-certified CPU:** The Cortex-M33 can be a safety island, and the whole chip supports functional safety.
- **Rich peripherals:** Multiple interfaces for sensors, displays, storage, and networking.

**Quick numbers**

claims: Subject: New edge-AI part: NXP i.MX 95
The i.MX 95 is a great fit for our edge-AI product.
It's the first i.MX to support functional safety with an Arm Cortex-M33, plus it has the NXP Energy Flex architecture for efficiency.
Arm Cortex-A55 (6 cores, up to 1.8 GHz), Cortex-M7 (1 core, up to 800 MHz), Cortex-M33 (1 core, up to 333 MHz)
1.8 GHz A55 + 800 MHz M7 + 333 MHz M33 in a single package
6400 MT/s LPDDR5 (19x19 mm package) or 4266 MT/s in LPDDR4X
3x uSDHC (SD3.0, SDIO3.0, eMMC5.1), 8x LPI2C, 8x LPSPI, 2x I3C, octal SPI, 4K OCRAM ECC
Secure features: EdgeLock secure enclave, tamper detection, secure clock, secure boot, crypto, eFuse key storage, random number generator
Four eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPUs, plus a Weight Decoder, Rescaler/Shifter, Activation Engine, and Buffers
On-chip accelerator for efficient machine-learning workloads (NN inference), working with the CPU for higher performance and lower power
Optimizes weights, manages memory accesses, provides rescaling, activation, and pooling functions
Supports 2D circular data buffer (Data Canvas) for data reuse among compute pipelines
Built-in DMA and Interconnect fabric for efficient memory-to-compute transfers
Low power:** The CPU and NPU share a 64 kB L2 cache, and the NPU has its own 1492 kB OCRAM (ECC).
The Neutron NPU also powers down when not in use.
High throughput:** Four NPUs plus optimized weight management and memory handling.
Software tooling:** eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU enablement is provided with the eIQ Toolkit and eIQ ML SDDE.
You can import your trained and quantized NN, and the tooling generates an NPU-optimized model.
Safety-certified CPU:** The Cortex-M33 can be a safety island, and the whole chip supports functional safety.
Rich peripherals:** Multiple interfaces for sensors, displays, storage, and networking.

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, what does the i.MX 95 Neutron NPU do, and what are its key features?
rows.raw:
The i.MX 95 Neutron NPU is the eIQ® Neutron N3-1024S NPU, an on-chip hardware accelerator that provides efficient processing of machine-learning workloads. It works in conjunction with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural-network (NN) inference.

Key features include:
- It handles Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) compute blocks throughput.
- It optimizes the arrangement of weights.
- It manages memory accesses.
- It provides rescaling, activation, and pooling functions.

The NPU supports various network types, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and more, with specific matrix sizes and operations listed in the reference manual.

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, what does the i.MX 95 Neutron NPU do, and what are its key features?
rows.raw:
The Neutron NPU is an on-chip hardware accelerator that provides efficient processing of machine-learning workloads. It works in conjunction with the chip's CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural-network (NN) inference. Its key features, from the i.MX 95 NPU Domain Overview, are:

- **Performance:** 2.0 TOP/s capability.
- **MACs and clocking:** 1024 MACs operating at up to 1.0 GHz and 2 OPS/MAC.
- **Memory:** 1 MB local SRAM.
- **Natively supported NN workloads:** Convolutional neural networks (CNN, including atrous separable convolution and depthwise separable convolutional networks with 1x1, 3x3, 5x5, and 7x7 matrix sizes, plus stride and padding support), recurrent neural networks (RNN, including MGU networks), and various activation functions (ReLU, PreLU, LeakyReLU), along with sampling/reshaping functions, element-wise operations,

**i.MX 95 Overview**
- Dual-core MC7/M33 with optional NPU (e.g. Neutron N3-1024S), Cortex-A55 CPU, Mali GPU, and 64kB L2 cache. Packages include 19x19 mm and 15x15 mm (1 PCIe and no 10GbE).
- Memory: 1492kB OCRAM (ECC), 32kB i-cache, 32kB d-cache, plus LPDDR5/LPDDR4X, SD/eMMC5.1, Octal SPI flash, 4x CAN-FD, 8-channel ADC, 6x UART/USART, 6x I2C, 6x SPI, 1x MIPI-DSI, 2x 1GbE (with TSN), 2x PCIe Gen 3.0 x12, 10GbE (with TSN).
- Security: EdgeLock Secure Enclave, tamper detection, battery-backed secure module domain, and inline PRINCE encryption.
- Clocks and power: coherent 512kB L3 cache (ECC), CCM, SRC, GPC, and a 150 MHz system clock.

**NPU**
- Optional with the Neutron N3-1024S (2x 4-lane or 1x 8-lane LVDS). It offers 256 MACs/cycle and runs machine learning models with the Cortex-A55's enhanced ARMv8.2-A instruction set.
- Memory-mapped, with 16kB of TCM/OCRAM (ECC).

**Memory/Connectivity**
- Main memory: 1492kB OCRAM (ECC), 32kB i-cache and 32kB d-cache, plus LPDDR5/LPDDR4X (inline ECC & encryption).
- High-speed I/O: 3x SD/SDIO3.0/eMMC5.1, 2x 1GbE (with TSN), 2x PCIe Gen 3.0 x12, 10GbE (with TSN).
- Display: 2x MIPI-CSI 4-lane (1 mux with DSI) and 1x MIPI-DSI 4-lane (with PHY).
- Audio: 2x 4-lane or 1x 8-lane LVDS, 2-lane I2S TDM Tx/Rx, SPDIF Tx/Rx.

**Target markets**
- Industrial: factory automation, robotics, IIoT gateways, edge AI/ML, smart energy, and connected devices.
- Consumer and commercial: smart home, POS, medical devices, and point-of-sale kiosks.

NOTE 11.3 SMMU-700 This chip supports ARM System-level Memory Management Unit (SMMU) SMMU-700 for memory management and conversion of virtual input address to physical output address. This translation is based on address mapping and memory attribute information that is available from configuration tables and translation tables that are stored in memory. SMMU can support up to two stages of translation: • One TCU in NoC domain • Three TBUs in Wakeup domain • One DTI interconnect (DTI_IC0) in Wakeup domain • Eight TBUs in NoC domain • One DTI interconnect (DTI_IC1) in NoC domain • Two AXI-4 Stream SSIs for the DTI interface between Wakeup domain: DTI_IC0 and NoC domain DTI_IC1 • SMMU performs translation table walks for each stage of translation and supports up to 48 bit VA (virtual address). • SMMU TTB1 table must be disabled using EPD1 (disable) fields in the Context Descriptor for the existence of TTB1 table. There is no sharing of the Cortex-A MMU tables and IO-SMMU translation tables. SMMU Bypass There are cases where the traffic must logically bypass the TBU.

Block diagram 107.1.2 Features Below is a list of features supported on iEP-RC: • Presents as a PCIe Root Complex that contains Event Collectors, and integrates with Integrated End Point (RCiEP or iEP) - For easy software discovery of peripheral functions and error reporting; leverage the infrastructure built into OSes and RTOS for PCIe. • Discoverable capabilities at a granular level - Software can discover what features/capabilities exists; allow an easy upgrade path. • 7'd2 ECAM buses to provide access to the PCIe Config space of the iEP and RCEC • 7'd2 Root Complex Event Collectors (RCEC) • Generate PCIe wired interrupt to the system on receiving error or Power Management Event message from iEP 107.1.3 PCI/PCIe Background It is useful to have an understanding of PCI/PCIe to be able to understand PCI Root Complex Integrated Endpoints. This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, generate a concise one-page product brief for the NXP i.MX 95: overview, NPU, memory/connectivity, and target markets.
rows.raw:
**NXP i.MX 95 Overview**
- Cortex-A55 CPU (single-core, up to 1.7 GHz) with ARMv8.2-A enhancements, including dedicated ML instructions
- First application processor with ARM Ethos-U65 microNPU, 256 MACs/cycle
- Cortex-M7 and Cortex-M33 cores
- Security: EdgeLock secure subsystem, PKC, public-key authentication, factory RoT programming, tamper detection, PUF options
- Up to 2MB flash and 512kB SRAM
- Supports up to 4GB LPDDR4/LPDDR4X, ECC, and internal flash encryption

**NPU (Ethos-U65)**
- 256 MACs/cycle
- On-chip memory (OCRAM_C with 64 KB blocks)
- Dedicated ML instructions in the Cortex-A55
- Secure boot and firmware update authentication in ROM

**Memory/Connectivity**
- Up to 4GB LPDDR4/LPDDR4X, ECC, and internal flash encryption
- Interfaces: MIPI DSI, LVDS, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C, SDIO, PCIe 2.0, USB 2.0, CAN-FD
- On-chip peripherals include ADC, DAC, PWM, I2S, and display interfaces
- High-performance graphics: up to 1200x1200@60Hz and 1080p@60Hz

**Target Markets**
- Industrial IoT, smart building, digital signage, point-of-sale, and medical devices
- Edge computing, factory automation, and smart home gateways

SMMU can support up to two stages of translation: • One TCU in NoC domain • Three TBUs in Wakeup domain • One DTI interconnect (DTI_IC0) in Wakeup domain • Eight TBUs in NoC domain • One DTI interconnect (DTI_IC1) in NoC domain • Two AXI-4 Stream SSIs for the DTI interface between Wakeup domain: DTI_IC0 and NoC domain DTI_IC1 • SMMU performs translation table walks for each stage of translation and supports up to 48 bit VA (virtual address). • SMMU TTB1 table must be disabled using EPD1 (disable) fields in the Context Descriptor for the existence of TTB1 table. Block diagram 107.1.2 Features Below is a list of features supported on iEP-RC: • Presents as a PCIe Root Complex that contains Event Collectors, and integrates with Integrated End Point (RCiEP or iEP) - For easy software discovery of peripheral functions and error reporting; leverage the infrastructure built into OSes and RTOS for PCIe. • Discoverable capabilities at a granular level - Software can discover what features/capabilities exists; allow an easy upgrade path. • 7'd2 ECAM buses to provide access to the PCIe Config space of the iEP and RCEC • 7'd2 Root Complex Event Collectors (RCEC) • Generate PCIe wired interrupt to the system on receiving error or Power Management Event message from iEP 107.1.3 PCI/PCIe Background It is useful to have an understanding of PCI/PCIe to be able to understand PCI Root Complex Integrated Endpoints. This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, generate a concise one-page product brief for the NXP i.MX 95: overview, NPU, memory/connectivity, and target markets.
rows.raw:
**i.MX 95 Overview**
- Cortex-A55 CPU up to 1.7 GHz, enhanced ARMv8.2-A with ML acceleration (Ethos-U65 microNPU)
- Industrial temperature, CAN-FD, 15-year longevity
- Code Watchdog, Intrusion and Tamper Response Controller, PUF, Tamper detection, glitch detection
- Security subsystems: EdgeLock, PKC, factory RoT programming

**NPU**
- Ethos-U65 microNPU with 256 MACs/cycle, integrated into the SoC
- Supports INT8/INT16 weights and activations, with an ML framework API
- Dedicated instructions for efficient matrix and vector math

**Memory/Connectivity**
- Up to 2 MB flash, 512 KB SRAM (sizes vary by part)
- LPDDR4/LPDDR4X with ECC, 16-bit memory interface
- PCIe integrated endpoint (NETC) with 7'd2 ECAM buses and 7'd2 RCECs
- Interfaces: MIPI DSI, LVDS, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C, SDIO, CAN, I3C, SAI, USB, Ethernet (QoS)

**Target Markets**
- Industrial: Energy Storage & Management, Smart Metering, Factory Automation, Industrial HMI
- Smart Home: Home Security & Surveillance, Smart Lighting, Smart Appliance Control, Smart Speaker, Soundbar
- Robotics: Motion Control, Brushless DC Motor Control, Predictive Maintenance
- Edge AI/ML: Anomaly Detection, Vision and Voice Recognition

Block diagram 107.1.2 Features Below is a list of features supported on iEP-RC: • Presents as a PCIe Root Complex that contains Event Collectors, and integrates with Integrated End Point (RCiEP or iEP) - For easy software discovery of peripheral functions and error reporting; leverage the infrastructure built into OSes and RTOS for PCIe. • Discoverable capabilities at a granular level - Software can discover what features/capabilities exists; allow an easy upgrade path. • 7'd2 ECAM buses to provide access to the PCIe Config space of the iEP and RCEC • 7'd2 Root Complex Event Collectors (RCEC) • Generate PCIe wired interrupt to the system on receiving error or Power Management Event message from iEP 107.1.3 PCI/PCIe Background It is useful to have an understanding of PCI/PCIe to be able to understand PCI Root Complex Integrated Endpoints. This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.
